fsspec-fuse Mount fsspec filesystems with FUSE Build Status codecov License PyPI Overview fsspec-fuse mounts an fsspec URL as a read-only local directory, so any program can list and read it with ordinary file operations. fsspec-fuse s3://my-bucket/reports /mnt/reports -o region=us-east-1 ls /mnt/reports URLs resolve through the filesystem registry that fsspec-rs shares between extensions. Native backends (file://, s3://, and protocols registered by packages such as fsspec-db and fsspec-kafka) run in Rust. Any other protocol falls back to the Python fsspec implementation installed for it, such as gcsfs or adlfs. From Python, mount returns a handle that unmounts on unmount() or when its with block ends: import os from fsspec_fuse import mount with mount("s3://my-bucket/reports", "/mnt/reports", region="us-east-1"): print(os.listdir("/mnt/reports")) Storage options pass to the backend as strings. threads sets how many requests the mount serves at once (default 4). Requirements Linux: FUSE 3 (fusermount3, from the fuse3 package on Debian and Ubuntu). macOS: macFUSE. Windows is not supported yet. Mounts are read-only.
